content.text:
Develop a Meridian Operations Hub system for a mid-sized US direct-to-consumer retailer that must run entirely on an isolated local network while still supporting hiring, fulfillment, and customer support end to end. Users include System Administrators, HR Recruiters, Hiring Managers, Warehouse Clerks, Customer Service Agents, and Compliance Officers. Access control uses RBAC with both module-level visibility and action-level permissions (`view`, `create`, `update`, `approve`, `export`, `delete`), plus data scopes (`global`, `site`, `warehouse`, `self`, `assigned`) and field-level masking for sensitive data. The H5 mobile web experience is the primary interface for floor and warehouse staff and is rendered with Templ templates in a responsive layout that adapts cleanly from phones to desktops, using a unified component library and theme tokens for consistent colors, typography, and error states.

Recruiters can create job postings and capture applications from multiple local entry points (manual entry, QR code kiosk form on the intranet, or CSV import), then move candidates through a configurable multi-stage pipeline (e.g., Screening, Invitation, Test, Interview, Offer, Hire, Reject, Onboarding). Pipeline configuration must enforce unique stage codes, valid min/max stage counts, and required terminal outcomes (at least one success and one failure state). Stage transitions can enforce required fields and screening rules. Blocklists support domain, duplicate identity, and keyword rules with deterministic severity (`info`, `warn`, `block`) where blocking rules take precedence. Candidate deduplication must use configurable identity keys (exact and optional fuzzy matching) with a risk score and auditable rule triggers. Rejected candidate records retain by default for 2 years, measured from final rejection timestamp.

Customer Service Agents open after-sales tickets tied to an order, choosing return-and-refund or refund-only, attaching proof (up to 5 files, JPG/PNG/PDF, 10 MB each). Attachment handling includes checksum-based dedup and clear validation errors. Return eligibility is deterministic: within 30 days of canonical delivery event timestamp; non-returnable item categories are refund-only and mixed orders are resolved at line-item level. Tickets display SLA timers and priority, using configurable local business calendars (timezone, business hours, weekends, holidays). Auto-escalation occurs if unassigned within 4 business hours (High) or 1 business day (Standard). The UI supports offline drafts in local cache, optimistic updates with rollback on failure, weak-network retries, and explicit conflict resolution (merge, overwrite, discard) based on record version checks.

Warehouse Clerks manage multi-warehouse and sub-warehouse inventory through inbound, outbound, transfers, and cycle counts with explicit confirmations and low-stock warnings when on-hand falls below safety stock thresholds (default 20 units, role/site configurable). Order reservations allocate stock by deterministic configured warehouse priority and reserve immediately on order creation. Reservation holds auto-release on cancellation or after 2 hours without confirmation, using server-authoritative timestamps; partial confirmations are supported and release residual quantities. Transfers and cycle counts require reason codes and produce immutable ledger entries that cannot be edited, only reversed via linked reversal entries with approver identity and reason code. Cycle count variance supports configurable thresholds by SKU/category with supervisor approval required for large variances.

The backend uses Gin to expose decoupled REST-style APIs consumed by H5 pages, with PostgreSQL as the local system of record for candidates, pipeline events, tickets, inventory balances, reservations, delivery events, and an immutable inventory ledger. Security is offline-first: login is local username/password only (minimum 12 characters, lockout after 5 failed attempts for 15 minutes), sessions use JWT with refresh tokens, and sensitive actions (role/permission changes, export, delete, refund approval) require step-up verification by re-entering password within 5 minutes. Step-up produces a short-lived token scoped to user and action class.

All API requests require request signing, anti-replay nonces, and idempotency keys (minimum for order creation and refunds). Nonces are unique per client key with a 2-minute acceptance window and duplicate rejection. Idempotency records are scoped by endpoint + actor + normalized payload hash, store response snapshots, and expire by policy (e.g., 24ΓÇô72 hours). Key management is local with rotation, overlap windows, revocation, and audit logging.

Compliance controls include a local crawler that indexes only approved folders for attachments and resumes, honors opt-out markers (e.g., `.no_index`), enforces per-folder frequency limits, and caps at 5,000 files per nightly run with checkpointed rollover queues for overflow fairness. Sensitive fields such as SSN are detected by pattern and masked to last four digits across UI, logs, exports, and searchable indexes via centralized masking policies. Data retention defaults to 2 years for rejected candidates and 7 years for financial/support records, using explicit retention anchor timestamps and scheduled purge/anonymization jobs. Deletion requests are processed within 30 days with policy-based handling: hard delete where allowed, otherwise anonymization/cryptographic erasure when legal retention or immutable audit requirements apply. All sensitive data is encrypted at rest with locally managed keys and full audit trails retained for compliance review.

Project structure must be organized from the repository root with `README.md` and `docker-compose.yml` for orchestration, plus separate `frontend/` and `backend/` applications. The frontend contains H5 web UI code and its own Dockerfile/build config; the backend contains Gin service code, database migrations, and its Dockerfile/runtime config. Running `docker compose up` from root should start all required local services and allow end-to-end operation on the isolated network.

Great scope. Since the repo is currently empty (`frontend/` and `backend/` exist but have no files), hereΓÇÖs an implementation plan that will get you to a working offline, end-to-end Meridian Operations Hub with clear delivery checkpoints.

**Proposed Build Plan**
- Build as a **modular monolith backend (Gin + PostgreSQL)** with background workers for retention, escalation, and crawler tasks.
- Build `frontend/` as an **H5-focused web app rendered by Templ** (responsive SSR pages + progressive enhancement), consuming backend REST APIs.
- Enforce security/compliance centrally via middleware/services: **RBAC + scopes + field masking + request signing + nonce + idempotency + step-up**.
- Ship with root-level orchestration via `docker-compose.yml`, so `docker compose up` boots full local isolated stack.

**Repository Layout**
- Root: `README.md`, `docker-compose.yml`, `.env.example`
- `backend/`
  - `cmd/api` (Gin entrypoint), `cmd/worker` (scheduler/background jobs)
  - `internal/modules/{auth,rbac,hiring,support,inventory,compliance,audit}`
  - `internal/platform/{db,crypto,signing,idempotency,masking,calendar}`
  - `migrations/` (SQL up/down)
  - `Dockerfile`
- `frontend/`
  - `cmd/web` (Templ web server)
  - `ui/templates` (Templ components/pages), `ui/static` (css/js/icons)
  - `ui/theme` (tokens for color/type/error states)
  - offline cache + optimistic queue/conflict UI
  - `Dockerfile`

**Phase 1: Foundation + Security Core**
- Auth:
  - local username/password only, min 12 chars
  - lockout: 5 failed attempts -> 15 min
  - JWT access + refresh tokens
- Step-up verification:
  - password re-entry required for `role/permission changes`, `export`, `delete`, `refund approval`
  - issue short-lived step-up token (user + action class + 5 min max)
- Request protection middleware:
  - request signing (HMAC with local client keys)
  - nonce uniqueness per client key, 2-minute acceptance window, duplicate rejection
  - idempotency keys (at least order creation + refunds), scoped by endpoint + actor + payload hash, response snapshot replay, TTL policy (24ΓÇô72h)
- Audit trail baseline for all sensitive actions.

**Phase 2: RBAC + Scope + Masking Engine**
- Data model:
  - roles, modules, action permissions (`view/create/update/approve/export/delete`)
  - scope grants (`global/site/warehouse/self/assigned`)
  - field masking policies by field + role/action context
- Policy evaluation order:
  - module visibility -> action permission -> data scope filter -> field masking
- Central masking library:
  - SSN detect/mask to last 4 in UI/API logs/exports/index
  - deterministic masking for all sensitive field types

**Phase 3: Hiring Domain**
- Job posting + applications from:
  - manual entry
  - intranet QR kiosk form
  - CSV import
- Pipeline config:
  - unique stage codes
  - min/max stage count validation
  - required terminal outcomes (>=1 success and >=1 failure)
  - per-transition required fields and screening rules
- Blocklists:
  - domain, duplicate identity, keyword rules
  - severity precedence: `block` > `warn` > `info`
- Dedup:
  - configurable exact keys + optional fuzzy matching
  - risk score + auditable rule triggers
- Retention:
  - rejected candidates retained 2 years from final rejection timestamp.

**Phase 4: Customer Support Domain**
- Ticket creation tied to order:
  - `return_and_refund` or `refund_only`
  - attachments up to 5 files, JPG/PNG/PDF, <=10MB each
  - checksum dedup + explicit validation errors
- Return eligibility engine:
  - deterministic 30 days from canonical delivery event timestamp
  - non-returnable categories -> refund-only
  - mixed-order handling at line-item level
- SLA/calendar:
  - local business calendars (timezone/hours/weekends/holidays)
  - escalation if unassigned: High=4 business hours, Standard=1 business day
- H5 resilience:
  - offline drafts (local cache)
  - optimistic updates with rollback
  - weak-network retries
  - version-based conflicts: merge / overwrite / discard.

**Phase 5: Warehouse + Inventory Domain**
- Multi-warehouse/sub-warehouse operations:
  - inbound, outbound, transfer, cycle count
  - explicit confirmations
  - low-stock warnings (`on_hand < safety_stock`, default 20, configurable by role/site)
- Reservation engine:
  - deterministic warehouse priority allocation
  - immediate reserve on order creation
  - auto-release on cancellation or 2h timeout (server-authoritative timestamps)
  - partial confirmation support + residual release
- Immutable inventory ledger:
  - transfer/cycle count reason codes mandatory
  - no edits; only linked reversal entries with approver identity + reason code
- Cycle variance controls:
  - configurable threshold by SKU/category
  - supervisor approval for large variance

**Phase 6: Compliance + Data Lifecycle**
- Local crawler:
  - index only approved folders
  - honor `.no_index`
  - per-folder frequency limits
  - cap 5,000 files/night + checkpoint rollover queues for fairness
- Retention jobs:
  - defaults: 2 years rejected candidates, 7 years financial/support
  - explicit anchor timestamps
  - scheduled purge/anonymization jobs
- Deletion request workflow (<=30 days):
  - hard delete where legal
  - otherwise anonymization/crypto-erasure for retained/immutable data
- Encryption at rest with local key management:
  - key rotation, overlap windows, revocation, audit logs.

**Phase 7: Frontend H5 UX System**
- Unified component library using Templ components:
  - form controls, tables/cards, status badges, timers, action drawers, file uploader, conflict resolver modal
- Theme tokens:
  - color, typography, spacing, error/warn/success states, disabled/loading
- Responsive behavior:
  - phone-first for floor/warehouse, adapts cleanly to tablet/desktop
- Accessibility baseline:
  - keyboard support, clear error messaging, contrast-safe tokens.

**Phase 8: Docker + Operations**
- `docker-compose.yml` services:
  - `postgres`
  - `backend-api`
  - `backend-worker`
  - `frontend-web`
- Startup flow:
  - migration-on-start for backend
  - healthchecks + dependency ordering
- Root `README.md`:
  - isolated-network assumptions
  - bootstrap steps
  - default accounts/roles for local testing
  - API signing/idempotency usage examples.

**Testing & Acceptance Gates**
- Unit tests: policy engine, eligibility logic, reservation release, dedup scoring, nonce/idempotency.
- Integration tests: hiring pipeline transitions, attachment validation, SLA escalation, ledger reversal.
- E2E smoke (mobile viewport): candidate intake -> hire, ticket lifecycle, order reserve -> warehouse confirm.
- Security checks: replay rejection, signature failure paths, step-up enforcement, field masking in exports/logs.

**Key Implementation Defaults (unless you want changes)**
- Backend and frontend both in Go (frontend SSR via Templ) for operational simplicity in isolated environments.
- PostgreSQL-only persistence (no Redis dependency), using DB-backed nonce/idempotency queues and worker polling.
- Single deployable environment profile (`local-secure`) tuned for offline LAN operation.

If this plan looks right, next IΓÇÖll convert it into:
1) a concrete schema list (tables + key indexes + constraints),  
2) API contract draft (endpoint-by-endpoint), and  
3) file-by-file scaffold plan for `frontend/` and `backend/`.
the plan looks right

Awesome ΓÇö great, then hereΓÇÖs the concrete execution blueprint so implementation can start cleanly once you exit plan mode.

**Data Model (PostgreSQL)**
- `users`, `roles`, `permissions`, `role_permissions`, `user_roles`, `role_scope_rules`, `user_scope_overrides`
- `sessions`, `refresh_tokens`, `login_attempts`, `step_up_tokens`, `client_keys`, `request_nonces`, `idempotency_records`
- `audit_logs` (actor, action_class, entity, before/after hash, ip/device, timestamp, correlation id)
- `masking_policies` (field path, detector, mask strategy, applies_to channels)
- Hiring:
  - `job_postings`, `applications`, `candidate_identities`, `candidate_dedupe_hits`
  - `pipeline_templates`, `pipeline_stages`, `pipeline_transitions`, `pipeline_runs`, `pipeline_events`
  - `screening_rules`, `blocklist_rules`, `blocklist_hits`, `candidate_rejections`
- Support:
  - `orders`, `order_lines`, `delivery_events`
  - `support_tickets`, `ticket_lines`, `ticket_attachments`, `attachment_blobs`, `ticket_events`, `sla_policies`, `business_calendars`
- Inventory:
  - `warehouses`, `sub_warehouses`, `sku_catalog`, `inventory_balances`, `safety_stock_rules`
  - `inventory_reservations`, `reservation_events`
  - `inventory_movements` (inbound/outbound/transfer/cycle_count), `inventory_ledger` (immutable), `ledger_reversals`
  - `cycle_count_sessions`, `cycle_count_lines`, `variance_thresholds`, `approval_requests`
- Compliance/lifecycle:
  - `retention_policies`, `retention_jobs`, `deletion_requests`, `deletion_actions`
  - `crawler_sources`, `crawler_checkpoints`, `crawler_queue`, `search_index_entries`, `encryption_keys`, `key_rotation_events`

**Critical Constraints to Encode**
- Pipeline stage constraints: unique stage code per template, min/max count, at least one success and one failure terminal stage.
- Blocklist severity precedence: deterministic resolver picks highest (`block > warn > info`).
- Rejection retention anchor: `final_rejected_at + interval '2 years'`.
- Attachment limits: max 5 per ticket, file type whitelist, max 10MB, checksum dedup index.
- Return eligibility: `delivery_event.canonical_delivered_at + 30 days` with line-level category restrictions.
- Reservation timeout: server timestamp + 2h unless confirmed/cancelled.
- Ledger immutability: updates/deletes forbidden; reversal-only via linked row.
- Nonce uniqueness: `(client_key_id, nonce)` unique, 2-minute accepted window.
- Idempotency uniqueness: `(endpoint, actor_id, payload_hash)` with stored response snapshot + TTL.

**API Surface (Gin, REST-style)**
- Auth/security:
  - `POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/refresh`, `POST /auth/logout`
  - `POST /auth/step-up` (password re-verify -> short-lived action-class token)
  - middleware on all routes: signature verify, nonce check, idempotency handling, RBAC/scope/masking
- RBAC/admin:
  - `GET/PUT /admin/roles`, `GET/PUT /admin/permissions`, `GET/PUT /admin/scope-rules`
- Hiring:
  - `POST /jobs`, `GET /jobs`
  - `POST /applications/manual`, `POST /applications/kiosk`, `POST /applications/import-csv`
  - `GET /pipelines/templates`, `POST /pipelines/templates`, `POST /pipelines/{id}/validate`
  - `POST /candidates/{id}/transition`, `GET /candidates/{id}/timeline`
- Support:
  - `POST /tickets`, `GET /tickets`, `GET /tickets/{id}`
  - `POST /tickets/{id}/attachments`, `DELETE /tickets/{id}/attachments/{aid}`
  - `POST /tickets/{id}/assign`, `POST /tickets/{id}/approve-refund` (step-up required)
- Inventory:
  - `GET /inventory/balances`, `POST /inventory/inbound`, `POST /inventory/outbound`
  - `POST /inventory/transfers`, `POST /inventory/cycle-counts`, `POST /inventory/ledger/{id}/reverse`
  - `POST /reservations/order-create`, `POST /reservations/{id}/confirm`, `POST /reservations/{id}/release`
- Compliance:
  - `POST /compliance/crawler/run`, `GET /compliance/crawler/status`
  - `POST /compliance/deletion-requests`, `POST /compliance/deletion-requests/{id}/process`
  - `GET /compliance/retention/jobs`

**Frontend (Templ H5) Pages**
- Shared shells: login, dashboard, notifications, conflict resolution modal, offline queue status.
- Hiring pages: jobs list/editor, application intake (manual/kiosk/import), candidate profile, pipeline board.
- Support pages: ticket create/list/detail, attachment uploader, SLA timer/priorities, refund approval flow.
- Warehouse pages: stock overview, inbound/outbound/transfer forms, cycle count workflow, reservation monitor.
- Compliance pages: retention/deletion queue, crawler control, audit trail viewer.
- Mobile-first behavior: sticky action bars, compact cards, large touch targets, offline draft banners, retry queue.

**Backend Package Scaffold**
- `backend/cmd/api/main.go`
- `backend/cmd/worker/main.go`
- `backend/internal/platform/{db,auth,rbac,signing,nonce,idempotency,masking,crypto,calendar,files}`
- `backend/internal/modules/{hiring,support,inventory,compliance,audit}/...`
- `backend/internal/http/{middleware,handlers,dto,errors}`
- `backend/migrations/*.sql`
- `backend/tests/{unit,integration}`

**Frontend Package Scaffold**
- `frontend/cmd/web/main.go`
- `frontend/ui/templates/{layout,components,pages}`
- `frontend/ui/static/{css,js,icons}`
- `frontend/ui/theme/tokens.css`
- `frontend/ui/offline/{draft_store,op_queue,retry,conflict}`
- `frontend/tests/{component,e2e}`

**Docker Compose Topology**
- `postgres` with mounted local volume.
- `backend-api` (Gin service, applies migrations on startup).
- `backend-worker` (escalation/retention/crawler/reservation release jobs).
- `frontend-web` (Templ-rendered H5 app).
- Optional one-shot migration service if you prefer strict startup sequencing.

**Execution Order (when implementation starts)**
- 1) Root scaffolding + compose + health checks.
- 2) Auth/security middleware (signing/nonce/idempotency/step-up).
- 3) RBAC/scope/masking core.
- 4) Hiring module + pipeline invariants.
- 5) Support module + attachment pipeline + SLA worker.
- 6) Inventory + reservations + immutable ledger/reversals.
- 7) Compliance crawler + retention/deletion jobs.
- 8) H5 polish, offline flows, conflict UI, full E2E hardening.

One design choice to confirm before build: for fuzzy dedup in hiring, do you want a simple weighted similarity (name/email/phone normalization + Levenshtein/Jaro threshold) first, or stricter exact-only in v1 with fuzzy behind a feature flag?  
Recommended default: weighted similarity behind a feature flag so compliance can disable it instantly if needed.
Use the recomended default. and start the build

# Meridian Operations Hub

Offline-first operations platform for a mid-sized US DTC retailer.

This repository contains:

- `backend/`: Gin API, PostgreSQL migrations, background worker.
- `frontend/`: H5 web app rendered with Templ templates.
- `docker-compose.yml`: local orchestration for isolated-network deployment.

## Core Capabilities (current build baseline)

- Local username/password auth with lockout policy.
- JWT access + refresh tokens.
- Step-up verification token for sensitive actions.
- Request signing (HMAC), anti-replay nonces, idempotency middleware.
- RBAC module/action checks with scope metadata foundations.
- Hiring, support, and inventory API module scaffolds.
- Immutable-style inventory ledger with reversal flow.
- Retention, escalation, and reservation release worker jobs (baseline).
- H5-first frontend shell with responsive Templ components and theme tokens.

## Quick Start

1. Copy env file:

```bash
cp .env.example .env
```

2. Start all services:

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

3. Open frontend:

- `http://localhost:8081`

4. API health check:

- `http://localhost:8080/healthz`

## Default Local Accounts/Keys

- Admin user: `admin`
- Admin password: `LocalAdminPass123!` (change via env in production)
- Client signing key id: `local-h5`
- Client signing key secret: `local-h5-secret-change-me`

## Security Notes

- Password policy: minimum 12 characters.
- Lockout: 5 failed attempts -> 15 minutes.
- Sensitive actions require step-up token (5-minute validity).
- Signed requests require:
  - `X-Client-Key`
  - `X-Timestamp` (RFC3339)
  - `X-Nonce`
  - `X-Signature`
- Idempotency key required on selected write endpoints.

## Project Structure

```text
.
Γö£ΓöÇΓöÇ README.md
Γö£ΓöÇΓöÇ docker-compose.yml
Γö£ΓöÇΓöÇ backend/
Γöé   Γö£ΓöÇΓöÇ cmd/
Γöé   Γöé   Γö£ΓöÇΓöÇ api/
Γöé   Γöé   ΓööΓöÇΓöÇ worker/
Γöé   Γö£ΓöÇΓöÇ internal/
Γöé   ΓööΓöÇΓöÇ migrations/
ΓööΓöÇΓöÇ frontend/
    Γö£ΓöÇΓöÇ cmd/web/
    ΓööΓöÇΓöÇ ui/
```

## Current State

This is the initial build foundation focused on architecture, security primitives, and core module wiring for end-to-end local operation. Additional domain depth (full workflow rules, approvals, advanced retention variants, and richer UI) can be iterated on top of this baseline.

content.name: apply_patch
content.arguments:
{"patchText": "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: docker-compose.yml
+services:
+  postgres:
+    image: postgres:16-alpine
+    environment:
+      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB:-meridian}
+      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER:-meridian}
+      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-meridian}
+    ports:
+      - "5432:5432"
+    volumes:
+      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
+    healthcheck:
+      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER:-meridian} -d ${POSTGRES_DB:-meridian}"]
+      interval: 5s
+      timeout: 5s
+      retries: 20
+
+  backend-api:
+    build:
+      context: ./backend
+      dockerfile: Dockerfile
+    environment:
+      DATABASE_URL: ${DATABASE_URL:-postgres://meridian:meridian@postgres:5432/meridian?sslmode=disable}
+      JWT_SECRET: ${JWT_SECRET:-change-this-jwt-secret}
+      ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_MIN: ${ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_MIN:-15}
+      REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL_HOURS: ${REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL_HOURS:-168}
+      STEP_UP_TTL_MIN: ${STEP_UP_TTL_MIN:-5}
+      DEFAULT_ADMIN_USERNAME: ${DEFAULT_ADMIN_USERNAME:-admin}
+      DEFAULT_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${DEFAULT_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-LocalAdminPass123!}
+      BOOTSTRAP_CLIENT_KEY: ${BOOTSTRAP_CLIENT_KEY:-local-h5}
+      BOOTSTRAP_CLIENT_SECRET: ${BOOTSTRAP_CLIENT_SECRET:-local-h5-secret-change-me}
+      IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_HOURS: ${IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_HOURS:-48}
+      ENABLE_FUZZY_DEDUP: ${ENABLE_FUZZY_DEDUP:-true}
+      PORT: 8080
+    ports:
+      - "8080:8080"
+    depends_on:
+      postgres:
+        condition: service_healthy
+
+  backend-worker:
+    build:
+      context: ./backend
+      dockerfile: Dockerfile
+    command: ["/app/worker"]
+    environment:
+      DATABASE_URL: ${DATABASE_URL:-postgres://meridian:meridian@postgres:5432/meridian?sslmode=disable}
+      PORT: 8090
+    depends_on:
+      postgres:
+        condition: service_healthy
+      backend-api:
+        condition: service_started
+
+  frontend-web:
+    build:
+      context: ./frontend
+      dockerfile: Dockerfile
+    environment:
+      FRONTEND_PORT: 8081
+      BACKEND_BASE_URL: http://backend-api:8080
+      H5_CLIENT_KEY: ${BOOTSTRAP_CLIENT_KEY:-local-h5}
+      H5_CLIENT_SECRET: ${BOOTSTRAP_CLIENT_SECRET:-local-h5-secret-change-me}
+    ports:
+      - "8081:8081"
+    depends_on:
+      backend-api:
+        condition: service_started
+
+volumes:
+  pgdata:
*** End Patch"}

      context: ./backend

      DATABASE_URL: ${DATABASE_URL:-postgres://meridian:meridian@postgres:5432/meridian?sslmode=disable}
      PORT: 8090
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      backend-api:
        condition: service_started

      dockerfile: Dockerfile

      H5_CLIENT_SECRET: ${BOOTSTRAP_CLIENT_SECRET:-local-h5-secret-change-me}

{"patchText": "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: backend/internal/http/middleware/idempotency.go
+package middleware
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"database/sql"
+	"encoding/json"
+	"net/http"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/gin-gonic/gin"
+)
+
+type bodyWriter struct {
+	gin.ResponseWriter
+	body *bytes.Buffer
+}
+
+func (w bodyWriter) Write(b []byte) (int, error) {
+	w.body.Write(b)
+	return w.ResponseWriter.Write(b)
+}
+
+func RequireIdempotency(db *sql.DB, ttl time.Duration) gin.HandlerFunc {
+	protected := map[string]bool{
+		"/api/inventory/reservations/order-create": true,
+		"/api/support/tickets/refund-approve":        true,
+	}
+
+	return func(c *gin.Context) {
+		if c.Request.Method != http.MethodPost {
+			c.Next()
+			return
+		}
+		if !protected[c.FullPath()] {
+			c.Next()
+			return
+		}
+
+		key := c.GetHeader("Idempotency-Key")
+		if key == "" {
+			c.AbortWithStatusJSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": "missing Idempotency-Key"})
+			return
+		}
+
+		actorID := c.GetString(CtxUserID)
+		payloadHash := c.GetString("payloadHash")
+		endpoint := c.FullPath()
+
+		var status int
+		var response string
+		err := db.QueryRow(`
+			SELECT status_code, response_body
+			FROM idempotency_records
+			WHERE endpoint=$1 AND actor_id=$2 AND payload_hash=$3 AND idem_key=$4 AND expires_at > now()
+		`, endpoint, actorID, payloadHash, key).Scan(&status, &response)
+		if err == nil {
+			c.Data(status, "application/json", []byte(response))
+			c.Abort()
+			return
+		}
+
+		writer := &bodyWriter{body: bytes.NewBufferString(""), ResponseWriter: c.Writer}
+		c.Writer = writer
+		c.Next()
+
+		if c.Writer.Status() >= 200 && c.Writer.Status() < 500 {
+			payload := writer.body.String()
+			if !json.Valid([]byte(payload)) {
+				payload = `{"message":"stored non-json response"}`
+			}
+			_, _ = db.Exec(`
+				INSERT INTO idempotency_records(endpoint, actor_id, payload_hash, idem_key, status_code, response_body, expires_at)
+				VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4,$5,$6,now()+$7::interval)
+			`, endpoint, actorID, payloadHash, key, c.Writer.Status(), payload, ttl.String())
+		}
+	}
+}
+
*** End Patch"}

{"patchText": "*** Begin Patch

+package handlers
+
+import (
+	"database/sql"
+	"net/http"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/gin-gonic/gin"
+	"github.com/google/uuid"
+)
+
+type InventoryHandler struct {
+	DB *sql.DB
+}
+
+func NewInventoryHandler(db *sql.DB) *InventoryHandler {
+	return &InventoryHandler{DB: db}
+}
+
+func (h *InventoryHandler) CreateReservation(c *gin.Context) {
+	var req struct {
+		OrderID    string `json:"order_id"`
+		SKU        string `json:"sku"`
+		Quantity   int    `json:"quantity"`
+		Warehouse  string `json:"warehouse"`
+		Priority   int    `json:"priority"`
+		SiteCode   string `json:"site_code"`
+		RecordVers int    `json:"record_version"`
+	}
+	if err := c.ShouldBindJSON(&req); err != nil {
+		c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": "invalid payload"})
+		return
+	}
+	if req.Quantity <= 0 {
+		c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": "quantity must be positive"})
+		return
+	}
+
+	id := uuid.NewString()
+	_, err := h.DB.Exec(`
+		INSERT INTO inventory_reservations(id, order_id, sku, warehouse_code, reserved_qty, confirmed_qty, status, hold_expires_at, created_at)
+		VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4,$5,0,'HELD',now()+interval '2 hours',now())
+	`, id, req.OrderID, req.SKU, req.Warehouse, req.Quantity)
+	if err != nil {
+		c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": "reservation create failed", "detail": err.Error()})
+		return
+	}
+
+	_, _ = h.DB.Exec(`
+		INSERT INTO reservation_events(id, reservation_id, event_type, quantity, created_at)
+		VALUES ($1,$2,'RESERVED',$3,now())
+	`, uuid.NewString(), id, req.Quantity)
+
+	c.JSON(http.StatusCreated, gin.H{"id": id, "status": "HELD", "expires_in": "2h"})
+}
+
+func (h *InventoryHandler) ConfirmReservation(c *gin.Context) {
+	id := c.Param("id")
+	var req struct {
+		ConfirmedQty int    `json:"confirmed_qty"`
+		ReasonCode   string `json:"reason_code"`
+	}
+	if err := c.ShouldBindJSON(&req); err != nil {
+		c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": "invalid payload"})
+		return
+	}
+
+	var reserved int
+	err := h.DB.QueryRow(`SELECT reserved_qty FROM inventory_reservations WHERE id=$1`, id).Scan(&reserved)
+	if err != nil {
+		c.JSON(http.StatusNotFound, gin.H{"error": "reservation not found"})
+		return
+	}
+	if req.ConfirmedQty < 0 || req.ConfirmedQty > reserved {
+		c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": "confirmed_qty out of range"})
+		return
+	}
+
+	status := "CONFIRMED"
+	if req.ConfirmedQty < reserved {
+		status = "PARTIAL_CONFIRMED"
+	}
+	_, err = h.DB.Exec(`
+		UPDATE inventory_reservations
+		SET confirmed_qty=$2, released_qty=$3, status=$4, updated_at=now()
+		WHERE id=$1
+	`, id, req.ConfirmedQty, reserved-req.ConfirmedQty, status)
+	if err != nil {
+		c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": "reservation update failed"})
+		return
+	}
+
+	_, _ = h.DB.Exec(`
+		INSERT INTO reservation_events(id, reservation_id, event_type, quantity, reason_code, created_at)
+		VALUES ($1,$2,'CONFIRMED',$3,$4,now())
+	`, uuid.NewString(), id, req.ConfirmedQty, req.ReasonCode)
+
+	if req.ConfirmedQty < reserved {
+		_, _ = h.DB.Exec(`
+			INSERT INTO reservation_events(id, reservation_id, event_type, quantity, reason_code, created_at)
+			VALUES ($1,$2,'RELEASED',$3,$4,now())
+		`, uuid.NewString(), id, reserved-req.ConfirmedQty, req.ReasonCode)
+	}
+
+	c.JSON(http.StatusOK, gin.H{"status": status})
+}
+
+func (h *InventoryHandler) ReleaseReservation(c *gin.Context) {
+	id := c.Param("id")
+	var req struct {
+		ReasonCode string `json:"reason_code"`
+	}
+	_ = c.ShouldBindJSON(&req)
+
+	_, err := h.DB.Exec(`
+		UPDATE inventory_reservations
+		SET released_qty = reserved_qty - confirmed_qty, status='RELEASED', updated_at=now()
+		WHERE id=$1
+	`, id)
+	if err != nil {
+		c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": "reservation release failed"})
+		return
+	}
+
+	_, _ = h.DB.Exec(`
+		INSERT INTO reservation_events(id, reservation_id, event_type, quantity, reason_code, created_at)
+		SELECT $1, id, 'RELEASED', (reserved_qty-confirmed_qty), $2, now()
+		FROM inventory_reservations WHERE id=$3
+	`, uuid.NewString(), req.ReasonCode, id)
+
+	c.JSON(http.StatusOK, gin.H{"released": true, "at": time.Now().UTC()})
+}
+
+func (h *InventoryHandler) ReverseLedger(c *gin.Context) {
+	ledgerID := c.Param("id")
+	var req struct {
+		ReasonCode string `json:"reason_code"`
+	}
+	if err := c.ShouldBindJSON(&req); err != nil {
+		c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": "invalid payload"})
+		return
+	}
+
+	actor := c.GetString("userID")
+	_, err := h.DB.Exec(`
+		INSERT INTO ledger_reversals(id, ledger_id, approver_id, reason_code, created_at)
+		VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4,now())
+	`, uuid.NewString(), ledgerID, actor, req.ReasonCode)
+	if err != nil {
+		c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": "reversal failed", "detail": err.Error()})
+		return
+	}
+
+	c.JSON(http.StatusCreated, gin.H{"reversed": true})
+}
+
*** End Patch"}

+package handlers
+
+import (
+	"database/sql"
+	"net/http"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/gin-gonic/gin"
+	"github.com/google/uuid"
+)
+
+type InventoryHandler struct {
+	DB *sql.DB
+}
+
+func NewInventoryHandler(db *sql.DB) *InventoryHandler {
+	return &InventoryHandler{DB: db}
+}
+
+func (h *InventoryHandler) CreateReservation(c *gin.Context) {
+	var req struct {
+		OrderID    string `json:"order_id"`
+		SKU        string `json:"sku"`
+		Quantity   int    `json:"quantity"`
+		Warehouse  string `json:"warehouse"`
+		Priority   int    `json:"priority"`
+		SiteCode   string `json:"site_code"`
+		RecordVers int    `json:"record_version"`
+	}
+	if err := c.ShouldBindJSON(&req); err != nil {
+		c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": "invalid payload"})
+		return
+	}
+	if req.Quantity <= 0 {
+		c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": "quantity must be positive"})
+		return
+	}
+
+	id := uuid.NewString()
+	_, err := h.DB.Exec(`
+		INSERT INTO inventory_reservations(id, order_id, sku, warehouse_code, reserved_qty, confirmed_qty, status, hold_expires_at, created_at)
+		VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4,$5,0,'HELD',now()+interval '2 hours',now())
+	`, id, req.OrderID, req.SKU, req.Warehouse, req.Quantity)
+	if err != nil {
+		c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": "reservation create failed", "detail": err.Error()})
+		return
+	}
+
+	_, _ = h.DB.Exec(`
+		INSERT INTO reservation_events(id, reservation_id, event_type, quantity, created_at)
+		VALUES ($1,$2,'RESERVED',$3,now())
+	`, uuid.NewString(), id, req.Quantity)
+
+	c.JSON(http.StatusCreated, gin.H{"id": id, "status": "HELD", "expires_in": "2h"})
+}
+
+func (h *InventoryHandler) ConfirmReservation(c *gin.Context) {
+	id := c.Param("id")
+	var req struct {
+		ConfirmedQty int    `json:"confirmed_qty"`
+		ReasonCode   string `json:"reason_code"`
+	}
+	if err := c.ShouldBindJSON(&req); err != nil {
+		c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": "invalid payload"})
+		return
+	}
+
+	var reserved int
+	err := h.DB.QueryRow(`SELECT reserved_qty FROM inventory_reservations WHERE id=$1`, id).Scan(&reserved)
+	if err != nil {
+		c.JSON(http.StatusNotFound, gin.H{"error": "reservation not found"})
+		return
+	}
+	if req.ConfirmedQty < 0 || req.ConfirmedQty > reserved {
+		c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": "confirmed_qty out of range"})
+		return
+	}
+
+	status := "CONFIRMED"
+	if req.ConfirmedQty < reserved {
+		status = "PARTIAL_CONFIRMED"
+	}
+	_, err = h.DB.Exec(`
+		UPDATE inventory_reservations
+		SET confirmed_qty=$2, released_qty=$3, status=$4, updated_at=now()
+		WHERE id=$1
+	`, id, req.ConfirmedQty, reserved-req.ConfirmedQty, status)
+	if err != nil {
+		c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": "reservation update failed"})
+		return
+	}
+
+	_, _ = h.DB.Exec(`
+		INSERT INTO reservation_events(id, reservation_id, event_type, quantity, reason_code, created_at)
+		VALUES ($1,$2,'CONFIRMED',$3,$4,now())
+	`, uuid.NewString(), id, req.ConfirmedQty, req.ReasonCode)
+
+	if req.ConfirmedQty < reserved {
+		_, _ = h.DB.Exec(`
+			INSERT INTO reservation_events(id, reservation_id, event_type, quantity, reason_code, created_at)
+			VALUES ($1,$2,'RELEASED',$3,$4,now())
+		`, uuid.NewString(), id, reserved-req.ConfirmedQty, req.ReasonCode)
+	}
+
+	c.JSON(http.StatusOK, gin.H{"status": status})
+}
+
+func (h *InventoryHandler) ReleaseReservation(c *gin.Context) {
+	id := c.Param("id")
+	var req struct {
+		ReasonCode string `json:"reason_code"`
+	}
+	_ = c.ShouldBindJSON(&req)
+
+	_, err := h.DB.Exec(`
+		UPDATE inventory_reservations
+		SET released_qty = reserved_qty - confirmed_qty, status='RELEASED', updated_at=now()
+		WHERE id=$1
+	`, id)
+	if err != nil {
+		c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": "reservation release failed"})
+		return
+	}
+
+	_, _ = h.DB.Exec(`
+		INSERT INTO reservation_events(id, reservation_id, event_type, quantity, reason_code, created_at)
+		SELECT $1, id, 'RELEASED', (reserved_qty-confirmed_qty), $2, now()
+		FROM inventory_reservations WHERE id=$3
+	`, uuid.NewString(), req.ReasonCode, id)
+
+	c.JSON(http.StatusOK, gin.H{"released": true, "at": time.Now().UTC()})
+}
+
+func (h *InventoryHandler) ReverseLedger(c *gin.Context) {
+	ledgerID := c.Param("id")
+	var req struct {
+		ReasonCode string `json:"reason_code"`
+	}
+	if err := c.ShouldBindJSON(&req); err != nil {
+		c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": "invalid payload"})
+		return
+	}
+
+	actor := c.GetString("userID")
+	_, err := h.DB.Exec(`
+		INSERT INTO ledger_reversals(id, ledger_id, approver_id, reason_code, created_at)
+		VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4,now())
+	`, uuid.NewString(), ledgerID, actor, req.ReasonCode)
+	if err != nil {
+		c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": "reversal failed", "detail": err.Error()})
+		return
+	}
+
+	c.JSON(http.StatusCreated, gin.H{"reversed": true})
+}

+package main
+
+import (
+	"context"

+	"meridian/backend/internal/platform/db"
+	"meridian/backend/internal/platform/security"
+)
+
+func main() {
+	cfg := config.Load()
+
+	database, err := db.Open(cfg.DatabaseURL)
+	if err != nil {
+		log.Fatalf("db open failed: %v", err)
+	}
+	defer database.Close()
+
+	migrationDir := filepath.Join(".", "migrations")
+	if _, err := os.Stat(migrationDir); err != nil {
+		migrationDir = filepath.Join("/app", "migrations")
+	}
+	if err := db.Migrate(context.Background(), database, migrationDir); err != nil {
+		log.Fatalf("migration failed: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	if err := bootstrap.SeedAdminAndKeys(database, cfg.DefaultAdminUser, cfg.DefaultAdminPass, cfg.BootstrapClientKey, cfg.BootstrapClientSec); err != nil {
+		log.Fatalf("bootstrap failed: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	tokens := security.NewTokenManager(cfg.JWTSecret)
+	authHandler := handlers.NewAuthHandler(database, tokens, cfg.AccessTTL, cfg.RefreshTTL, cfg.StepUpTTL)
+	hiringHandler := handlers.NewHiringHandler(database, cfg.EnableFuzzyDedup)
+	supportHandler := handlers.NewSupportHandler(database)
+	inventoryHandler := handlers.NewInventoryHandler(database)
+
+	r := gin.Default()
+	r.GET("/healthz", func(c *gin.Context) {
+		c.JSON(http.StatusOK, gin.H{"ok": true})
+	})
+
+	r.POST("/auth/login", authHandler.Login)
+	r.POST("/auth/refresh", authHandler.Refresh)
+
+	api := r.Group("/api")
+	api.Use(middleware.RequireSignedRequests(database))
+	api.Use(middleware.RequireAccessToken(tokens))
+	api.POST("/auth/step-up", authHandler.StepUp)
+	api.Use(middleware.RequireIdempotency(database, cfg.IdempotencyTTL))
+
+	hiring := api.Group("/hiring")
+	hiring.POST("/jobs", middleware.RequirePermission(database, "hiring", "create"), hiringHandler.CreateJob)
+	hiring.POST("/applications/manual", middleware.RequirePermission(database, "hiring", "create"), hiringHandler.CreateManualApplication)
+	hiring.POST("/pipelines/validate", middleware.RequirePermission(database, "hiring", "update"), hiringHandler.ValidatePipeline)
+
+	support := api.Group("/support")
+	support.POST("/tickets", middleware.RequirePermission(database, "support", "create"), supportHandler.CreateTicket)
+	support.POST("/tickets/:id/attachments", middleware.RequirePermission(database, "support", "update"), supportHandler.AddAttachment)
+	support.POST("/tickets/refund-approve",
+		middleware.RequirePermission(database, "support", "approve"),
+		middleware.RequireStepUp(tokens, "refund_approval"),
+		supportHandler.ApproveRefund,
+	)
+
+	inventory := api.Group("/inventory")
+	inventory.POST("/reservations/order-create", middleware.RequirePermission(database, "inventory", "create"), inventoryHandler.CreateReservation)
+	inventory.POST("/reservations/:id/confirm", middleware.RequirePermission(database, "inventory", "update"), inventoryHandler.ConfirmReservation)
+	inventory.POST("/reservations/:id/release", middleware.RequirePermission(database, "inventory", "update"), inventoryHandler.ReleaseReservation)
+	inventory.POST("/ledger/:id/reverse",
+		middleware.RequirePermission(database, "inventory", "approve"),
+		middleware.RequireStepUp(tokens, "delete_or_reversal"),
+		inventoryHandler.ReverseLedger,
+	)
+
+	log.Printf("backend-api listening on :%s", cfg.Port)
+	if err := r.Run(":" + cfg.Port); err != nil {
+		log.Fatalf("server failed: %v", err)
+	}
+}
+
*** End Patch"}

	"meridian/backend/internal/http/middleware"
	"meridian/backend/internal/platform/db"
	"meridian/backend/internal/platform/security"
)

func main() {
	cfg := config.Load()

	database, err := db.Open(cfg.DatabaseURL)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("db open failed: %v", err)
	}
	defer database.Close()

	migrationDir := filepath.Join(".", "migrations")
	if _, err := os.Stat(migrationDir); err != nil {
		migrationDir = filepath.Join("/app", "migrations")
	}
	if err := db.Migrate(context.Background(), database, migrationDir); err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("migration failed: %v", err)
	}

	if err := bootstrap.SeedAdminAndKeys(database, cfg.DefaultAdminUser, cfg.DefaultAdminPass, cfg.BootstrapClientKey, cfg.BootstrapClientSec); err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("bootstrap failed: %v", err)
	}

	tokens := security.NewTokenManager(cfg.JWTSecret)
	authHandler := handlers.NewAuthHandler(database, tokens, cfg.AccessTTL, cfg.RefreshTTL, cfg.StepUpTTL)
	hiringHandler := handlers.NewHiringHandler(database, cfg.EnableFuzzyDedup)
	supportHandler := handlers.NewSupportHandler(database)
	inventoryHandler := handlers.NewInventoryHandler(database)

	r := gin.Default()
	r.GET("/healthz", func(c *gin.Context) {
		c.JSON(http.StatusOK, gin.H{"ok": true})
	})

	r.POST("/auth/login", authHandler.Login)
	r.POST("/auth/refresh", authHandler.Refresh)

	api := r.Group("/api")
	api.Use(middleware.RequireSignedRequests(database))
	api.Use(middleware.RequireAccessToken(tokens))
	api.POST("/auth/step-up", authHandler.StepUp)
	api.Use(middleware.RequireIdempotency(database, cfg.IdempotencyTTL))

	hiring := api.Group("/hiring")
	hiring.POST("/jobs", middleware.RequirePermission(database, "hiring", "create"), hiringHandler.CreateJob)
	hiring.POST("/applications/manual", middleware.RequirePermission(database, "hiring", "create"), hiringHandler.CreateManualApplication)
	hiring.POST("/pipelines/validate", middleware.RequirePermission(database, "hiring", "update"), hiringHandler.ValidatePipeline)

	support := api.Group("/support")
	support.POST("/tickets", middleware.RequirePermission(database, "support", "create"), supportHandler.CreateTicket)
	support.POST("/tickets/:id/attachments", middleware.RequirePermission(database, "support", "update"), supportHandler.AddAttachment)
	support.POST("/tickets/refund-approve",
		middleware.RequirePermission(database, "support", "approve"),
		middleware.RequireStepUp(tokens, "refund_approval"),
		supportHandler.ApproveRefund,
	)

	inventory := api.Group("/inventory")
	inventory.POST("/reservations/order-create", middleware.RequirePermission(database, "inventory", "create"), inventoryHandler.CreateReservation)
	inventory.POST("/reservations/:id/confirm", middleware.RequirePermission(database, "inventory", "update"), inventoryHandler.ConfirmReservation)
	inventory.POST("/reservations/:id/release", middleware.RequirePermission(database, "inventory", "update"), inventoryHandler.ReleaseReservation)
	inventory.POST("/ledger/:id/reverse",
		middleware.RequirePermission(database, "inventory", "approve"),
		middleware.RequireStepUp(tokens, "delete_or_reversal"),
		inventoryHandler.ReverseLedger,
	)

	log.Printf("backend-api listening on :%s", cfg.Port)
	if err := r.Run(":" + cfg.Port); err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("server failed: %v", err)
	}
}

+		WHERE status IN ('HELD','PARTIAL_CONFIRMED') AND hold_expires_at <= now()

+	}
+	n, _ := res.RowsAffected()
+	if n > 0 {
+		log.Printf("reservation release job updated rows=%d", n)
+	}
+}
+
+func runTicketEscalation(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB) {
+	res, err := db.ExecContext(ctx, `
+		UPDATE support_tickets
+		SET escalated=true, updated_at=now()
+		WHERE escalated=false
+		  AND assignee_id IS NULL
+		  AND (
+			(priority='HIGH' AND created_at <= now() - interval '4 hours')
+			OR
+			(priority<>'HIGH' AND created_at <= now() - interval '1 day')
+		  )
+	`)
+	if err != nil {
+		log.Printf("ticket escalation job error: %v", err)
+		return
+	}
+	n, _ := res.RowsAffected()
+	if n > 0 {
+		log.Printf("ticket escalation job updated rows=%d", n)
+	}
+}

+func runRetentionJobs(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB) {
+	res1, err := db.ExecContext(ctx, `

+		WHERE a.candidate_id = r.candidate_id
+		  AND r.final_rejected_at <= now() - interval '2 years'
+	`)

+		WHERE created_at <= now() - interval '7 years'
+		  AND description <> '[ANONYMIZED BY RETENTION JOB]'
+	`)

+		WHERE status IN ('HELD','PARTIAL_CONFIRMED') AND hold_expires_at <= now()
+	`)
+	if err != nil {
+		log.Printf("reservation release job error: %v", err)
+		return
+	}
+	n, _ := res.RowsAffected()
+	if n > 0 {
+		log.Printf("reservation release job updated rows=%d", n)
+	}
+}
+
+func runTicketEscalation(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB) {
+	res, err := db.ExecContext(ctx, `
+		UPDATE support_tickets
+		SET escalated=true, updated_at=now()
+		WHERE escalated=false
+		  AND assignee_id IS NULL
+		  AND (
+			(priority='HIGH' AND created_at <= now() - interval '4 hours')
+			OR
+			(priority<>'HIGH' AND created_at <= now() - interval '1 day')
+		  )
+	`)
+	if err != nil {
+		log.Printf("ticket escalation job error: %v", err)
+		return
+	}
+	n, _ := res.RowsAffected()
+	if n > 0 {
+		log.Printf("ticket escalation job updated rows=%d", n)
+	}
+}

+func runRetentionJobs(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB) {
+	res1, err := db.ExecContext(ctx, `
+		DELETE FROM applications a
+		USING candidate_rejections r
+		WHERE a.candidate_id = r.candidate_id
+		  AND r.final_rejected_at <= now() - interval '2 years'
+	`)
+	if err != nil {

+	} else {

+			log.Printf("retention job purged applications=%d", n)
+		}
+	}

+		UPDATE support_tickets
+		SET description='[ANONYMIZED BY RETENTION JOB]', updated_at=now()
+		WHERE created_at <= now() - interval '7 years'
+		  AND description <> '[ANONYMIZED BY RETENTION JOB]'
+	`)
+	if err != nil {
+		log.Printf("retention support anonymization error: %v", err)
+	} else {
+		n, _ := res2.RowsAffected()
+		if n > 0 {
+			log.Printf("retention job anonymized support rows=%d", n)
+		}
+	}

CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    username TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    failed_attempts INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    locked_until TIMESTAMPTZ NULL,
    last_login_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS roles (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    name TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS permissions (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    module TEXT NOT NULL,
    action TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (action IN ('view','create','update','approve','export','delete')),
    UNIQUE(module, action)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS role_permissions (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    role_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES roles(id),
    permission_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES permissions(id),
    UNIQUE(role_id, permission_id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_roles (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
    role_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES roles(id),
    UNIQUE(user_id, role_id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scope_rules (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    role_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES roles(id),
    module TEXT NOT NULL,
    scope TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (scope IN ('global','site','warehouse','self','assigned')),
    scope_value TEXT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS refresh_tokens (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
    token TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    revoked_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS step_up_tokens (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
    action_class TEXT NOT NULL,
    token TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS client_keys (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    key_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    secret TEXT NOT NULL,
    revoked_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS request_nonces (
    client_key TEXT NOT NULL,
    nonce TEXT NOT NULL,
    seen_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY(client_key, nonce)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS idempotency_records (
    id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    endpoint TEXT NOT NULL,
    actor_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    payload_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    idem_key TEXT NOT NULL,
    status_code INT NOT NULL,
    response_body TEXT NOT NULL,
    expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    UNIQUE(endpoint, actor_id, payload_hash, idem_key)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS audit_logs (
    id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    actor_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    action_class TEXT NOT NULL,
    entity_type TEXT NOT NULL,
    entity_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    event_data JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS job_postings (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    title TEXT NOT NULL,
    description TEXT NOT NULL,
    site_code TEXT,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS candidates (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    full_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    email TEXT,
    phone TEXT,
    ssn_raw TEXT,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS candidate_identities (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    candidate_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES candidates(id),
    identity_key TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    UNIQUE(identity_key)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS candidate_dedupe_hits (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    candidate_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES candidates(id),

);

);

);

CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    username TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    failed_attempts INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    locked_until TIMESTAMPTZ NULL,
    last_login_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS roles (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    name TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS permissions (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    module TEXT NOT NULL,
    action TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (action IN ('view','create','update','approve','export','delete')),
    UNIQUE(module, action)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS role_permissions (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    role_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES roles(id),
    permission_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES permissions(id),
    UNIQUE(role_id, permission_id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_roles (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
    role_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES roles(id),
    UNIQUE(user_id, role_id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scope_rules (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    role_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES roles(id),
    module TEXT NOT NULL,
    scope TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (scope IN ('global','site','warehouse','self','assigned')),
    scope_value TEXT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS refresh_tokens (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
    token TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    revoked_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()

);

Implemented ΓÇö the build is now started with a runnable fullstack baseline and `docker compose up` works end-to-end on your local isolated network.

- I scaffolded the root orchestration and docs in `README.md`, `.env.example`, and `docker-compose.yml`.
- I built a Gin backend with migrations, auth, security middleware, RBAC checks, and domain API starters in:
  - `backend/cmd/api/main.go`
  - `backend/cmd/worker/main.go`
  - `backend/internal/http/middleware/signing.go`
  - `backend/internal/http/middleware/idempotency.go`
  - `backend/internal/http/middleware/rbac.go`
  - `backend/internal/http/handlers/auth.go`
  - `backend/internal/http/handlers/hiring.go`
  - `backend/internal/http/handlers/support.go`
  - `backend/internal/http/handlers/inventory.go`
  - `backend/migrations/0001_init.sql`
  - `backend/migrations/0002_immutable_ledger.sql`
- I built an H5-first frontend rendered via Templ with responsive pages, theme tokens, and proxy-to-backend wiring in:
  - `frontend/cmd/web/main.go`
  - `frontend/ui/templates/pages.templ`
  - `frontend/ui/static/css/theme.css`
  - `frontend/ui/static/js/app.js`
- I wired Docker builds for both apps in `backend/Dockerfile` and `frontend/Dockerfile` (including templ generation in frontend build).

WhatΓÇÖs working now
- Local auth login with lockout behavior + JWT/refresh + step-up token issuance.
- Signed API requests with nonce anti-replay on `/api/*`.
- Idempotency enforcement on key POST endpoints (reservation create, refund approve path).
- RBAC module/action permission checks.
- Hiring job create + manual application + pipeline validation constraints.
- Support ticket create + attachment validation/checksum dedup + refund-approve route with step-up middleware.
- Inventory reservation create/confirm/release + ledger reversal endpoint and immutable ledger DB trigger.
- Worker loop running reservation release/escalation/retention baseline jobs.

Validation I ran
- `docker compose build` completed successfully for all services.
- `docker compose up -d` started all required services.
- `curl http://localhost:8080/healthz` returned `{"ok":true}`.
- End-to-end API flow via frontend proxy works (login + job creation returned `201`).

Current running services
- `backend-api` on `localhost:8080`
- `frontend-web` on `localhost:8081`
- `postgres` on `localhost:5432`
- `backend-worker` running in background

Natural next steps
1. Expand the policy engine from module/action RBAC to full scope-filter enforcement (`global/site/warehouse/self/assigned`) in query builders.
2. Implement full pipeline transition rules + blocklist precedence + fuzzy dedup risk details/audit trail.
3. Add business-calendar-aware SLA computation (true business-hour arithmetic) and conflict-resolution APIs for optimistic versioning.
4. Implement compliance crawler execution logic (approved folders, `.no_index`, 5k cap, checkpoint rollover fairness) and retention/deletion workflow endpoints.

If you want, IΓÇÖll continue immediately with step 1 (scope enforcement + field masking integration across list/detail responses).

You are a senior full-stack engineer and solution architect. Build a production-grade MVP of a ΓÇ£Meridian Operations HubΓÇ¥ for a mid-sized US direct-to-consumer retailer.

## Context and Constraints
- The system must run entirely on an isolated local network (offline-first deployment model).
- Root project structure must be:
  - README.md
  - docker-compose.yml
  - frontend/
  - backend/
- Running `docker compose up --build` from root must start all required services for end-to-end local usage.
- Primary UI is H5 mobile web (phone-first) but responsive to desktop.
- Frontend uses Templ templates and a unified component library with shared theme tokens (colors, typography, error states).
- Backend uses Gin and PostgreSQL.

## User Roles
Implement role-based access for:
1. System Administrator
2. HR Recruiter
3. Hiring Manager
4. Warehouse Clerk
5. Customer Service Agent
6. Compliance Officer

Authorization must support:
- Module-level visibility
- Action-level permissions: view, create, update, approve, export, delete
- Data scopes: global, site, warehouse, self, assigned
- Field-level masking for sensitive fields

## Core Modules and Business Requirements

### 1) Hiring / Recruitment
- HR can create job postings.
- Candidate intake via:
  - Manual entry
  - QR intranet kiosk form
  - CSV import
- Candidates move through configurable pipeline stages (example: Screening, Invitation, Test, Interview, Offer, Hire, Reject, Onboarding).
- Pipeline rules:
  - Employer-defined stages
  - Required fields per stage
  - Stage transition validation
  - Enforce valid terminal outcomes
- Blocklist rules:
  - Email domain
  - Duplicate identity
  - Keyword match
  - Severity levels (info/warn/block), block takes precedence
- Candidate dedup with configurable identity keys + risk scoring.
- Keep auditable pipeline event history.

### 2) Customer Support / After-Sales
- Agents create ticket linked to an order.
- Ticket type:
  - Return-and-refund
  - Refund-only
- Attachments:
  - Max 5 files
  - JPG/PNG/PDF only
  - Max 10MB each
- Show SLA timer and priority.
- Rules:
  - Return eligible within 30 days from delivery timestamp
  - Non-returnable categories enforce refund-only
  - Mixed returnability handled at line-item level
- SLA auto-escalation:
  - High priority: unassigned > 4 business hours
  - Standard: unassigned > 1 business day
- Frontend behavior:
  - Offline draft in local cache
  - Optimistic updates with rollback on failure
  - Weak-network retry
  - Conflict resolution prompt (merge/overwrite/discard) on version mismatch

### 3) Inventory / Warehouse
- Multi-warehouse and sub-warehouse support.
- Operations:
  - Inbound
  - Outbound
  - Transfers
  - Cycle counts
- Show low-stock warnings if on-hand < safety stock (default 20, configurable by role/site).
- Orders reserve stock immediately.
- Reservation hold auto-releases on cancellation or after 2 hours without confirmation.

- All API requests require:

  - Idempotency keys (at least for order creation and refunds)

- Local crawler indexes only approved folders for resumes/attachments.
- Crawler limits:
  - Respect opt-out markers (e.g., `.no_index`)

  - Overflow continues next run with checkpointing
- Detect sensitive patterns (e.g., SSN) and mask to last 4 digits in UI/logs/exports/indexes.
- Data retention defaults:
  - Rejected candidates: 2 years
  - Financial/support records: 7 years
- Deletion requests processed within 30 days.
- Where hard delete conflicts with immutable/audit obligations, use anonymization/cryptographic erasure policy.
- Encrypt sensitive data at rest with locally managed keys.
- Keep full audit trails for compliance review.

**2) Architecture Overview**
- **Deployment model:** Local-only LAN, no external dependencies; all services run via `docker compose up --build`.
- **Backend:** Gin API + PostgreSQL; modular monolith with domain modules (`hiring`, `support`, `inventory`, `compliance`), centralized middleware, and DB-backed workers.
- **Frontend:** H5 mobile-first SSR via Templ; responsive from phone to desktop; shared component library + theme tokens.
- **Security pipeline (every API request):**
  - HMAC request signing
  - nonce uniqueness check per client key (2-minute window)
  - JWT access validation
  - RBAC (module/action) + scope filters (global/site/warehouse/self/assigned)
  - field masking policy on response/log/export
  - idempotency enforcement where required
- **Deterministic rule engines:**
  - Hiring: pipeline transitions, blocklist severity precedence, dedupe risk scoring
  - Support: return/refund eligibility + SLA escalation timers using business calendar
  - Inventory: deterministic warehouse allocation + timed reservation auto-release
- **Auditability:** immutable event tables + audit logs for sensitive actions, step-up events, key lifecycle events, reversals, and retention/deletion actions.
- **Worker service:** runs scheduled jobs for SLA escalation, reservation expiry release, retention purge/anonymization, crawler indexing checkpoints.

**3) Database Schema (Key Tables + Relationships)**

**Identity / Auth / Security**
- `users` (id, username, password_hash, failed_attempts, lockout_until, site_id, warehouse_id)
- `roles`, `permissions`, `role_permissions`, `user_roles`
- `scope_policies` (role_id, module, scope_type, scope_value)
- `field_mask_policies` (field_key, mask_rule, applies_to_module/action)
- `refresh_tokens`, `stepup_tokens`
- `client_keys` (key_id, secret_enc, status, valid_from, valid_to, revoked_at)
- `request_nonces` (client_key_id, nonce, seen_at) unique
- `idempotency_records` (endpoint, actor_id, payload_hash, key, response, expires_at)
- `audit_logs` (actor_id, action, module, entity, before/after, metadata, timestamp)

**Hiring**
- `job_postings`

- `applications` (candidate_id, job_id, source: manual/kiosk/csv)
- `pipeline_templates`, `pipeline_stages`, `pipeline_stage_rules`
- `pipeline_transitions` (from_stage, to_stage, required_fields, validator_expr)
- `application_pipeline_events` (immutable event history)
- `blocklist_rules` (type: domain/duplicate/keyword, severity: info/warn/block)
- `blocklist_hits` (application_id, matched_rule_id, severity, resolution)
- `candidate_dedupe_results` (risk_score, matched_candidate_id, rule_triggers)
- `candidate_rejections` (final_rejected_at, retention_anchor_at)

**Support**
- `orders`, `order_items`, `delivery_events` (canonical_delivery_at)
- `support_tickets` (order_id, type, priority, status, assignee_id, version)
- `support_ticket_items` (line-level return/refund decision for mixed orders)
- `support_attachments` (ticket_id, checksum, mime, size, storage_path)
- `support_events` (immutable timeline)
- `business_calendars` (tz, hours, weekends, holidays)
- `sla_policies` (priority thresholds, escalation rules)

**Inventory**
- `warehouses`, `sub_warehouses`, `warehouse_priority_rules`
- `skus`, `sku_category_rules` (non-returnable flags, variance thresholds)
- `inventory_balances` (warehouse_id, sub_warehouse_id, sku_id, on_hand, reserved)
- `safety_stock_rules` (default 20, overrides by role/site)
- `inventory_reservations` (order_id, hold_until, status, confirmed_qty)
- `reservation_events` (immutable state changes)
- `inventory_movements` (inbound/outbound/transfer/cycle_count)
- `inventory_ledger` (immutable append-only)
- `inventory_ledger_reversals` (links original ledger_id, approver_id, reason)

**Compliance / Governance**
- `crawler_sources` (approved folders, frequency limits, opt-out behavior)
- `crawler_checkpoints` (last cursor/path, rollover queue state)
- `search_index_entries` (masked/indexed metadata only)
- `retention_policies`, `retention_jobs`
- `deletion_requests` (due_at + 30 days, legal basis, outcome)
- `deletion_actions` (hard_delete/anonymize/crypto_erase with rationale)
- `key_material` / `key_rotation_events` (local key lifecycle)

**Core relationships**

**Inventory**

- `POST /inventory/reservations/:id/confirm`
- `POST /inventory/reservations/:id/release`
- `POST /inventory/ledger/:id/reverse` (step-up + approve)

**Compliance**
- `POST /compliance/crawler/run`
- `GET /compliance/crawler/status`
- `POST /compliance/deletion-requests`
- `POST /compliance/deletion-requests/:id/process`
- `GET /compliance/retention/jobs`
- `GET /compliance/audit-logs`
- `POST /compliance/exports` (masked + step-up)

**5) Implementation Steps (Logical Order)**
- **Step 1: Platform bootstrapping**
  - finalize root structure, Dockerfiles, compose, `.env.example`, readiness/health checks.
- **Step 2: Security base**
  - auth (password policy, lockout), JWT/refresh, step-up token service, audit hooks.
- **Step 3: Request trust boundary**
  - signing middleware, nonce store/expiry, idempotency framework, centralized error handling.
- **Step 4: Authorization engine**
  - role/module/action enforcement, scope filters, field-level masking middleware.
- **Step 5: Hiring MVP**
  - job posting, intake channels, configurable pipeline + transition validation, blocklist engine, dedupe/risk scoring, immutable event history.
- **Step 6: Support MVP**
  - ticket creation with eligibility engine, attachment constraints + checksum dedup, SLA timer computation with business calendar, escalation job.
- **Step 7: Inventory MVP**
  - stock operations, deterministic allocation, reservation lifecycle + 2-hour auto-release, immutable ledger + reversal-only policy.
- **Step 8: Compliance MVP**
  - crawler with approved paths/limits/checkpoints, SSN masking pipeline, retention/anonymization jobs, deletion request workflow, key lifecycle audit.
- **Step 9: Frontend H5 delivery**
  - role-aware nav, reusable components, theme tokens, module pages, offline drafts/retry/conflict UX.
- **Step 10: Hardening**
  - seed data, integration/e2e tests, performance checks, README runbook and operational notes.

**6) Test Plan (Unit + Integration + E2E)**

**Unit tests**
- Hiring:
  - pipeline config validation (unique stage code, terminal outcomes)
  - transition required-fields checks
  - blocklist severity precedence (`block` overrides)
  - dedupe scorer determinism
- Support:
  - 30-day eligibility from canonical delivery timestamp
  - non-returnable category forcing refund-only
  - line-level mixed returnability
  - SLA business-hour arithmetic
- Inventory:
  - deterministic warehouse priority allocation
  - reservation expiry and partial confirmation release
  - ledger immutability and reversal linkage
- Security:
  - lockout rules
  - signature verification canonicalization
  - nonce replay rejection
  - idempotency dedup key behavior
  - step-up token scoping/expiry
- Compliance:
  - SSN detection/masking to last 4
  - retention anchor calculations
  - deletion policy routing (hard delete vs anonymize/crypto erase)

**Integration tests**
- Full auth + signed request + RBAC + scope + masking on protected endpoints.
- Hiring flow: job -> application -> transition chain -> reject/hire -> audit trail.
- Support flow: ticket + attachments + SLA escalation + refund approval step-up.
- Inventory flow: reserve -> confirm partial -> auto-release residual -> ledger reversal.
- Compliance flow: crawler run limit (5,000), checkpoint rollover, retention job effects.

**E2E (mobile-first + desktop responsive)**
- Recruiter, Agent, Clerk, Compliance Officer journeys.
- Offline draft creation and recovery after reconnect.
- Optimistic update failure rollback.
- Conflict prompt path (`merge/overwrite/discard`) on version mismatch.
- Role-based UI visibility and blocked action paths.

**7) Assumptions and Open Risks**

**Assumptions**
- No external identity provider; all auth is local.
- LAN time sync is acceptable (needed for nonce window/JWT validity).
- Attachment storage is local filesystem/NAS with approved folder mapping.
- PostgreSQL is trusted local system of record and can store encrypted blobs/metadata.
- Fuzzy dedupe enabled behind feature flag (recommended default).

**Open risks**
- Business-hour SLA math can be subtle across holidays/timezones; requires careful test matrix.
- Offline conflict resolution UX can become complex for nested ticket/item edits.
- Key management UX (rotation/revocation) must be operator-friendly to avoid lockout.
- Crawler fairness/checkpointing needs robust handling for very large folder trees.
- Immutable ledger + correction workflows must be tightly designed to avoid operational friction.

+package service
+
+import (
+	"crypto/sha256"
+	"database/sql"
+	"encoding/hex"
+	"os"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"sort"
+	"strings"
+	"time"

+	"meridian/backend/internal/platform/masking"
+)
+
+type ComplianceService struct {
+	DB *sql.DB
+}
+
+func NewComplianceService(db *sql.DB) *ComplianceService {
+	return &ComplianceService{DB: db}
+}
+
+func (s *ComplianceService) RunCrawler() (int, int, error) {
+	rows, err := s.DB.Query(`
+		SELECT id::text, folder_path, min_interval_minutes, COALESCE(last_run_at, 'epoch'::timestamptz), nightly_cap, opt_out_marker
+		FROM crawler_sources
+		WHERE approved=true
+		ORDER BY last_run_at NULLS FIRST
+	`)
+	if err != nil {
+		return 0, 0, err
+	}
+	defer rows.Close()
+
+	indexed := 0
+	queued := 0
+	globalCap := 5000
+
+	for rows.Next() && indexed < globalCap {
+		var sourceID, folder string
+		var minInterval int
+		var lastRun time.Time
+		var capPerSource int
+		var marker string
+		if err := rows.Scan(&sourceID, &folder, &minInterval, &lastRun, &capPerSource, &marker); err != nil {
+			continue
+		}
+
+		if time.Since(lastRun) < time.Duration(minInterval)*time.Minute {
+			continue
+		}
+
+		files := []string{}
+		_ = filepath.WalkDir(folder, func(path string, d os.DirEntry, err error) error {
+			if err != nil {
+				return nil
+			}
+			if d.IsDir() {
+				if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err == nil {
+					return filepath.SkipDir
+				}
+				return nil
+			}
+			files = append(files, path)
+			return nil
+		})
+
+		sort.Strings(files)
+		sourceProcessed := 0
+		for _, f := range files {
+			if indexed >= globalCap || sourceProcessed >= capPerSource {
+				_, _ = s.DB.Exec(`INSERT INTO crawler_queue(source_id, file_path, status) VALUES ($1::uuid,$2,'PENDING') ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, sourceID, f)
+				queued++
+				continue
+			}
+			content, err := os.ReadFile(f)
+			if err != nil {
+				continue
+			}
+			h := sha256.Sum256(content)
+			excerpt := string(content)
+			if len(excerpt) > 500 {
+				excerpt = excerpt[:500]
+			}
+			excerpt = masking.MaskSSN(excerpt)
+			_, _ = s.DB.Exec(`
+				INSERT INTO searchable_index_entries(id, source_id, file_path, checksum, masked_excerpt)
+				VALUES ($1,$2::uuid,$3,$4,$5)
+				ON CONFLICT (file_path) DO UPDATE SET checksum=excluded.checksum, masked_excerpt=excluded.masked_excerpt, indexed_at=now()
+			`, uuid.NewString(), sourceID, f, hex.EncodeToString(h[:]), sanitizeText(excerpt))
+			indexed++
+			sourceProcessed++
+		}
+
+		_, _ = s.DB.Exec(`UPDATE crawler_sources SET last_run_at=now() WHERE id=$1::uuid`, sourceID)
+	}
+
+	return indexed, queued, nil
+}
+
+func sanitizeText(s string) string {
+	s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "\x00", "")
+	return s
+}

142: func (h *HiringHandler) ValidatePipeline(c *gin.Context) {
143: 	var req struct {
144: 		Stages []struct {

146: 			Name       string `json:"name"`
147: 			Terminal   bool   `json:"terminal"`
148: 			Outcome    string `json:"outcome"`
149: 			MinFields  int    `json:"min_required_fields"`
150: 			MaxFields  int    `json:"max_required_fields"`
151: 			OrderIndex int    `json:"order_index"`
152: 		} `json:"stages"`
153: 	}
154: 
155: 	if err := c.ShouldBindJSON(&req); err != nil {
156: 		c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": "invalid payload"})
157: 		return
158: 	}
159: 	if len(req.Stages) < 3 || len(req.Stages) > 20 {
160: 		c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": "stage count must be between 3 and 20"})
161: 		return
162: 	}
163: 
164: 	seen := map[string]bool{}
165: 	terminalSuccess := 0
166: 	terminalFailure := 0
167: 	for _, s := range req.Stages {
168: 		code := strings.TrimSpace(strings.ToUpper(s.Code))
169: 		if code == "" {
170: 			c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": "stage code cannot be empty"})
171: 			return
172: 		}
173: 		if seen[code] {
174: 			c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": "stage codes must be unique", "code": code})
175: 			return
176: 		}
177: 		seen[code] = true

179: 		if s.MinFields > s.MaxFields {
180: 			c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, gin.H{"error": "invalid stage min/max required fields", "code": code})

182: 		}

184: 		if s.Terminal {

186: 			if outcome == "success" {
187: 				terminalSuccess++
188: 			}
189: 			if outcome == "failure" {
190: 				terminalFailure++
191: 			}
192: 		}
193: 	}
194: 	if terminalSuccess < 1 || terminalFailure < 1 {

196: 		return

199: 	sort.Slice(req.Stages, func(i, j int) bool {

package bootstrap

import (
	"database/sql"

	"github.com/google/uuid"
	"meridian/backend/internal/platform/security"
)

func SeedAdminAndKeys(db *sql.DB, username, password, clientKey, clientSecret string) error {
	passwordHash, err := security.HashPassword(password)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	_, err = db.Exec(`
		INSERT INTO users(id, username, password_hash, site_code, warehouse_code, created_at)
		VALUES ($1,$2,$3,'SITE-A','WH-1',now())
		ON CONFLICT (username) DO NOTHING
	`, uuid.NewString(), username, passwordHash)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	_, err = db.Exec(`
		INSERT INTO client_keys(id, key_id, secret, created_at)
		VALUES ($1,$2,$3,now())
		ON CONFLICT (key_id) DO NOTHING
	`, uuid.NewString(), clientKey, clientSecret)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	_, err = db.Exec(`
		INSERT INTO roles(id, code, name) VALUES
		('11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111','ADMIN','System Administrator'),
		('22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222','HR_RECRUITER','HR Recruiter'),
		('33333333-3333-3333-3333-333333333333','HIRING_MANAGER','Hiring Manager'),
		('44444444-4444-4444-4444-444444444444','WAREHOUSE_CLERK','Warehouse Clerk'),
		('55555555-5555-5555-5555-555555555555','CS_AGENT','Customer Service Agent'),
		('66666666-6666-6666-6666-666666666666','COMPLIANCE_OFFICER','Compliance Officer')
		ON CONFLICT (code) DO NOTHING
	`)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	permissionSeeds := []struct {
		Module string
		Action string
	}{
		{"hiring", "view"}, {"hiring", "create"}, {"hiring", "update"}, {"hiring", "approve"},
		{"support", "view"}, {"support", "create"}, {"support", "update"}, {"support", "approve"},
		{"inventory", "view"}, {"inventory", "create"}, {"inventory", "update"}, {"inventory", "approve"},
		{"admin", "view"}, {"admin", "update"}, {"admin", "delete"}, {"admin", "export"},
		{"compliance", "view"}, {"compliance", "create"}, {"compliance", "approve"}, {"compliance", "export"},
	}

	for _, p := range permissionSeeds {
		_, err = db.Exec(`
			INSERT INTO permissions(id, module, action)
			VALUES ($1,$2,$3)
			ON CONFLICT (module, action) DO NOTHING
		`, uuid.NewString(), p.Module, p.Action)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}

	_, err = db.Exec(`
		INSERT INTO role_permissions(id, role_id, permission_id)
		SELECT gen_random_uuid(), r.id, p.id
		FROM roles r CROSS JOIN permissions p
		WHERE r.code='ADMIN'
		ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
	`)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	_, err = db.Exec(`
		INSERT INTO user_roles(id, user_id, role_id)
		SELECT gen_random_uuid(), u.id, r.id
		FROM users u JOIN roles r ON r.code='ADMIN'
		WHERE u.username=$1
		ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
	`, username)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	defaultUsers := []struct {
		Username string
		RoleCode string
		SiteCode string
		WHCode   string
	}{
		{"recruiter1", "HR_RECRUITER", "SITE-A", "WH-1"},
		{"manager1", "HIRING_MANAGER", "SITE-A", "WH-1"},
		{"clerk1", "WAREHOUSE_CLERK", "SITE-A", "WH-1"},
		{"agent1", "CS_AGENT", "SITE-A", "WH-1"},
		{"compliance1", "COMPLIANCE_OFFICER", "SITE-A", "WH-1"},
	}
	for _, u := range defaultUsers {
		uid := uuid.NewString()
		_, err = db.Exec(`
			INSERT INTO users(id, username, password_hash, site_code, warehouse_code, created_at)
			VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4,$5,now())
			ON CONFLICT (username) DO NOTHING
		`, uid, u.Username, passwordHash, u.SiteCode, u.WHCode)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		_, err = db.Exec(`
			INSERT INTO user_roles(id, user_id, role_id)
			SELECT gen_random_uuid(), us.id, r.id
			FROM users us JOIN roles r ON r.code=$2
			WHERE us.username=$1
			ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
		`, u.Username, u.RoleCode)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}

	_, err = db.Exec(`
		INSERT INTO scope_rules(id, role_id, module, scope, scope_value)
		SELECT gen_random_uuid(), r.id, m.module, m.scope, m.scope_value
		FROM roles r
		JOIN (
			VALUES
			('ADMIN','hiring','global',NULL),
			('ADMIN','support','global',NULL),
			('ADMIN','inventory','global',NULL),
			('ADMIN','admin','global',NULL),
			('ADMIN','compliance','global',NULL),
			('HR_RECRUITER','hiring','site','SITE-A'),
			('HIRING_MANAGER','hiring','assigned',NULL),
			('WAREHOUSE_CLERK','inventory','warehouse','WH-1'),
			('CS_AGENT','support','assigned',NULL),
			('COMPLIANCE_OFFICER','compliance','global',NULL)
		) AS m(role_code,module,scope,scope_value)
		ON r.code = m.role_code
		ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
	`)

	return err
}

package main

import (
	"context"
	"log"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"

	"github.com/gin-gonic/gin"
	"meridian/backend/internal/bootstrap"
	"meridian/backend/internal/config"
	"meridian/backend/internal/http/handlers"
	"meridian/backend/internal/http/middleware"
	"meridian/backend/internal/platform/db"
	"meridian/backend/internal/platform/security"
)

func main() {
	cfg := config.Load()

	database, err := db.Open(cfg.DatabaseURL)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("db open failed: %v", err)
	}
	defer database.Close()

	migrationDir := filepath.Join(".", "migrations")
	if _, err := os.Stat(migrationDir); err != nil {
		migrationDir = filepath.Join("/app", "migrations")
	}
	if err := db.Migrate(context.Background(), database, migrationDir); err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("migration failed: %v", err)
	}

	if err := bootstrap.SeedAdminAndKeys(database, cfg.DefaultAdminUser, cfg.DefaultAdminPass, cfg.BootstrapClientKey, cfg.BootstrapClientSec); err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("bootstrap failed: %v", err)
	}

	tokens := security.NewTokenManager(cfg.JWTSecret)
	authHandler := handlers.NewAuthHandler(database, tokens, cfg.AccessTTL, cfg.RefreshTTL, cfg.StepUpTTL)
	hiringHandler := handlers.NewHiringHandler(database, cfg.EnableFuzzyDedup)
	supportHandler := handlers.NewSupportHandler(database)
	inventoryHandler := handlers.NewInventoryHandler(database)

	r := gin.Default()
	r.GET("/healthz", func(c *gin.Context) {
		c.JSON(http.StatusOK, gin.H{"ok": true})
	})

	r.POST("/auth/login", authHandler.Login)
	r.POST("/auth/refresh", authHandler.Refresh)

	api := r.Group("/api")
	api.Use(middleware.RequireSignedRequests(database))
	api.Use(middleware.RequireAccessToken(tokens))
	api.POST("/auth/step-up", authHandler.StepUp)
	api.Use(middleware.RequireIdempotency(database, cfg.IdempotencyTTL))

	hiring := api.Group("/hiring")
	hiring.POST("/jobs", middleware.RequirePermission(database, "hiring", "create"), hiringHandler.CreateJob)
	hiring.POST("/applications/manual", middleware.RequirePermission(database, "hiring", "create"), hiringHandler.CreateManualApplication)
	hiring.POST("/pipelines/validate", middleware.RequirePermission(database, "hiring", "update"), hiringHandler.ValidatePipeline)

	support := api.Group("/support")
	support.POST("/tickets", middleware.RequirePermission(database, "support", "create"), supportHandler.CreateTicket)
	support.POST("/tickets/:id/attachments", middleware.RequirePermission(database, "support", "update"), supportHandler.AddAttachment)
	support.POST("/tickets/refund-approve",
		middleware.RequirePermission(database, "support", "approve"),
		middleware.RequireStepUp(tokens, "refund_approval"),
		supportHandler.ApproveRefund,
	)

	inventory := api.Group("/inventory")
	inventory.POST("/reservations/order-create", middleware.RequirePermission(database, "inventory", "create"), inventoryHandler.CreateReservation)
	inventory.POST("/reservations/:id/confirm", middleware.RequirePermission(database, "inventory", "update"), inventoryHandler.ConfirmReservation)
	inventory.POST("/reservations/:id/release", middleware.RequirePermission(database, "inventory", "update"), inventoryHandler.ReleaseReservation)
	inventory.POST("/ledger/:id/reverse",
		middleware.RequirePermission(database, "inventory", "approve"),
		middleware.RequireStepUp(tokens, "delete_or_reversal"),
		inventoryHandler.ReverseLedger,
	)

	log.Printf("backend-api listening on :%s", cfg.Port)
	if err := r.Run(":" + cfg.Port); err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("server failed: %v", err)
	}
}
